01 — About

Built for the
hard problems.

I'm Chandana - and honestly, data engineering found me by accident. What started as pure frustration watching a broken ETL pipeline take down a production dashboard at 2am turned into a full-blown obsession. Turns out there's something deeply satisfying about why systems break at scale - and even more satisfying about building ones that don't.

At Databricks India, I spent 3+ years in the engine room: reverse-engineering bottlenecks in Spark execution plans, designing lakehouse architectures that processed terabytes without blinking, and building pipelines that earned zero complaints because they simply never failed. The milliseconds I shaved off ETL jobs weren't lucky - they were deliberate. Now I'm an MS student at UT Dallas, adding the analytical layer that turns good pipelines into smart ones.

Based in the United States, open to relocation anywhere. F-1 with 3 years STEM OPT - no sponsorship required.

03 — Projects

Things I've
built and broken.

Personal Project
🍸
Medallion Data Pipeline

A production-grade Bronze / Silver / Gold lakehouse architecture built from scratch. Raw data lands messy in Bronze. Silver cleanses, conforms, and dedduplicates it. Gold delivers curated, analytics-ready datasets - each layer immutable, observable, and fault-tolerant. Designed to absorb schema evolution without breaking downstream consumers.

View on GitHub ↗

Implements Delta Lake for ACID transaction guarantees, incremental processing with auto-detected change data capture, and automated data quality checks between layers that reject bad records before they ever reach analysts. The kind of pipeline that runs quietly at 4am and earns exactly zero pages.

04 — Beyond the Pipeline

The human behind
the data.

🏔
Hiking addict
Trails are my debugging sessions. Something about moving uphill with no Wi-Fi forces your brain to actually think. Yosemite, Grand Canyon - the list keeps growing and the ambitions keep escalating. I've decided I will reach Everest Base Camp before I retire. Not the summit - I'm ambitious, not unhinged. Just the base camp, the altitude headache, and the extremely dramatic photo.
Yosemite, CA
Grand Canyon, AZ
🧘
Yoga + running
Yoga for the calm. Running for the chaos. Zone 2 cardio is basically the data engineering of fitness - boring on the surface, building something serious underneath. My favorite runs are the ones where I'm convinced I'm dying and then somehow finish fine.
🎮
Certified PS5 gremlin
When the terminal is closed and the pipelines are all green, I disappear into deep PS5 sessions with zero guilt. Gaming taught me more about system design than I'd like to admit - also that I have an unhealthy competitive streak that transfers disturbingly well to debugging.
📚
Perpetual student
Currently deep in Apache Kafka, dbt, and advanced SQL window functions. I genuinely enjoy the feeling of being bad at something new - it means there's something interesting ahead. The learning stack never empties, and that's exactly how I like it.
⚡
Why data engineering?
A broken ETL at 2am is what got me. Most people would be frustrated and go to sleep. I got obsessed with why it broke, and then spent the next three years making sure it could never break that way again. That curiosity-meets-stubbornness is basically my whole career strategy.
